reasons.moat: Creative/document workflows and file formats are deeply embedded; $27.5B ARR and 1B+ monthly users across the platform.
reasons.disruption: Generative-AI tools and AI-native rivals (Figma, Canva) attack the core creative franchise; a soft Q4 guide revived those fears.
reasons.industry: Leader in creative software but facing more capable challengers; pricing power is being tested.
reasons.demand: Low-teens revenue growth and ~11% ARR growth; AI-first ARR (>$650M) growing >150% but still small.
reasons.management: Heavy buybacks; CEO transition (Shantanu Narayen to Anil Chakravarthy, Dec 1 2026) adds execution uncertainty.
reasons.tail_risk: Net cash, recurring subscription revenue, record operating cash flow.
reasons.catalyst: New CEO strategy, Firefly/agentic monetisation; fiscal 2027 guide in December.

bull_case: A cash-rich, still-growing franchise priced at ~12x earnings as if AI will erode it; if AI features lift ARPU instead, the multiple re-rates.
bear_case: AI lowers the skill barrier Adobe's moat rests on; growth decays toward single digits and the low multiple is deserved.
key_risk: Seat and pricing erosion as AI-native design tools take share of new creators.
catalyst_note: December fiscal-2027 guidance under the new CEO; AI-first ARR trajectory.

reasons.moat: Scale and US Gulf Coast refining advantage plus integrated MPLX midstream; still a commodity margin business.
reasons.disruption: EV and efficiency gains erode gasoline demand slowly; diesel and jet are stickier.
reasons.industry: Global refining capacity offline is supporting margins, but new capacity and restarts can reverse that.
reasons.demand: Long-run fuel demand flat to declining; current earnings reflect a cyclical margin spike (Q3 adj. EPS $26.93 vs $3.01 a year ago).
reasons.management: Returning cash aggressively ($3.3B in Q3) and sold two inland refineries for $4.2B near peak margins.
reasons.tail_risk: Margin mean-reversion risk is large; climate-litigation exposure.
reasons.catalyst: Management expects elevated margins at least to mid-2027; MPLX growth and asset-sale proceeds.

bull_case: Peak-cycle cash is being converted into buybacks at speed; if margins stay elevated into 2027, per-share value compounds.
bear_case: Earnings are near a cyclical peak; when cracks normalise, EPS could fall by more than half and the stock re-rates down.
key_risk: Refining margins normalising faster than expected.
catalyst_note: Q4 crack spreads and 2027 margin commentary; close of the refinery sale at end-2026.

reasons.moat: One of three DRAM producers with HBM technology leadership, but memory has historically been a commodity.
reasons.disruption: Memory is a binding constraint for AI systems; low risk of the product becoming obsolete.
reasons.industry: Three-player oligopoly; most 2027 HBM supply contracted at higher prices and >75% of fiscal-2027 shipments committed.
reasons.demand: AI infrastructure demand; management expects supply to tighten further through 2028.
reasons.management: Executing well in the upcycle; heavy capacity investment is the usual source of the next downturn.
reasons.tail_risk: Gross margins near 87% are far above history; capacity additions after fiscal 2027 could flip pricing.
reasons.catalyst: Fiscal Q1 2027 guide ($61.5B revenue) well above consensus; HBM4 ramp.

bull_case: Long-term contracts and AI demand make this cycle longer and higher than past ones, so peak-looking earnings persist.
bear_case: Memory remains cyclical; industry capex responds to 87% margins and pricing collapses in 2028-29.
key_risk: Supply response (Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron's own expansion) ending the shortage.

reasons.moat: Global hotel and rental supply plus a B2B technology platform; consumer brands are weaker than Booking's.
reasons.disruption: AI agents and Google's AI search could disintermediate online travel agencies; the company lists AI platforms as a competitive risk.
reasons.industry: Effectively a duopoly with Booking, with Google and Airbnb as powerful adjacent players.
reasons.demand: Travel demand resilient; B2B bookings +19% and revenue +23% in Q3 2026; consumer bookings +7%.
reasons.management: Margin expansion (adj. EBITDA +135bp) and a ~4% lower share count from buybacks.
reasons.tail_risk: Travel is cyclical; heavy marketing spend needed to hold consumer share.
reasons.catalyst: 2026 guidance raised; AI distribution partnerships (Google AI Mode) could open a new channel.

bull_case: B2B is becoming the travel industry's supply backbone, which AI agents need, so Expedia benefits rather than loses.
bear_case: AI assistants book direct with hotels or via Google, and the consumer business shrinks while marketing costs rise.
key_risk: Disintermediation of consumer bookings by AI platforms.
catalyst_note: Q4 results and 2027 outlook (February); AI-channel booking data.

reasons.moat: A price-taking oil and gas producer whose edges are limited to Egypt concession relationships, a Permian position smaller than larger rivals', and a carried interest in Suriname.
reasons.disruption: Oil and gas faces a slow energy-transition threat rather than near-term obsolescence; Egyptian gas serves as a bridge fuel for regional and European demand.
reasons.industry: Pricing is set by the global commodity market and OPEC+; Permian consolidation (including APA's Callon deal) has improved discipline, but no producer has pricing power.
reasons.demand: Realized oil of about $92/bbl in Q3 2026, up roughly 37% year over year, looks like a cyclical high; long-run oil demand is flat to declining and 2027 production is guided flat.
reasons.management: Recently disciplined ($2.8B of debt cut since end-2024, at least 60% of free cash flow returned, $500M cost program), offset by a long-tenured CEO with a mixed record on M&A and write-downs.
reasons.tail_risk: Net debt of about $3.2B plus a $782M decommissioning contingency on previously sold Gulf properties; Egypt brings political and production-sharing exposure, and earnings are geared to an elevated oil price.
reasons.catalyst: Net debt target of about $3B by year-end 2026 and Alaska exploration wells in 2027; GranMorgu first oil (mid-2028) falls outside the 12-month window.

bull_case: High oil prices and Permian outperformance lifted the 2026 free cash flow outlook to about $2.9B, funding quick deleveraging and heavy buybacks. Suriname's GranMorgu offers a funded, carried growth leg from 2028.
bear_case: Q3 earnings reflect roughly $92 oil; a reversion would squeeze free cash flow just as 2027 capital rises about $400M with flat production. Egypt dry holes, production-sharing dilution and legacy decommissioning liabilities add downside.
key_risk: Oil prices falling from cyclically elevated levels while capex rises for Suriname and exploration.
catalyst_note: Net debt target by year-end 2026; Alaska exploration and appraisal wells in 2027; GranMorgu first oil mid-2028.

reasons.moat: A two-sided B2B marketplace for large-parcel goods (about 1,500 sellers and 13,800 buyers) backed by roughly 35 fulfillment centers gives some network and logistics advantage, but it is contestable.
reasons.disruption: The shift of furniture sales online helps, but Amazon and Wayfair (also its channels) or sellers going direct could bypass the platform.
reasons.industry: The 10-K describes online large-parcel commerce as fragmented and fast-changing; third-party sellers compete with its own inventory and product margins slipped to 29.4% in Q3.
reasons.demand: Trailing marketplace GMV grew 24%, but US organic product growth is around 5% against a soft housing and furniture backdrop, and Europe is slowing.
reasons.management: Highly profitable with a $120M buyback, offset by dual-class founder control, a shrinking New Classic acquisition and a $2.75M class-action settlement over its AI claims.
reasons.tail_risk: About $418M of cash and investments and no debt, against tariff exposure on Asian sourcing, a Hong Kong/PRC structure with auditor-inspection delisting risk, and freight-dependent service margins.
reasons.catalyst: No dated event beyond routine Q4 results; Q4 guidance of $425-450M implies growth slowing to roughly 17-24%.

bull_case: Record Q3 with revenue up 27% to $423.6M, GMV and active buyers and sellers each growing over 20%, a debt-free balance sheet and ongoing buybacks. Europe and retail-partner sourcing add further growth avenues.
bear_case: Recent margin gains lean on a freight-rate spread management says it cannot forecast, while product margins compress and operating cash flow fell as inventory built. Tariff and China-structure risks could cap the valuation.
key_risk: Margin reversal if ocean freight spreads normalize while tariffs and third-party competition erode product margins.
catalyst_note: No dated event beyond Q4 2026 results in early 2027; Europe and retail-partner traction have unclear timing.

reasons.moat: Mostly commodity refining with some regional advantage from inland Rockies and Mid-Continent plants and a lubricants brand; not the industry's low-cost leader.
reasons.disruption: EVs and renewable fuels threaten long-run gasoline and diesel demand, but slowly; it also has its own renewable diesel exposure.
reasons.industry: US capacity has shrunk by roughly 630k bpd since 2019 with little new investment, which helps, but margins remain volatile in a commodity business.
reasons.demand: Q3 2026 margins ran about 2.8x a year earlier on geopolitical supply disruptions, which looks like a cyclical peak; consensus sees earnings falling sharply by 2029.
reasons.management: Steady returns ($572M in Q3, mostly buybacks) and sensible portfolio moves (Mississauga base-oil closure, Lubricants spin-off), but buying back near peak earnings and a CEO handover on 1 Jan 2027.
reasons.tail_risk: Modestly net cash ($3.33B cash vs $2.77B debt), but earnings lean on discretionary EPA small-refinery waivers and there is tariff exposure on Canadian crude.
reasons.catalyst: Dated CEO transition on 1 Jan 2027; Lubricants & Specialties spin-off planned during 2027 with timing within 12 months unclear.

bull_case: Shrinking US capacity and European import dependence could keep crack spreads above historical averages into 2027-28, sustaining large free cash flow for buybacks while the Lubricants spin-off surfaces value.
bear_case: Q3 2026 results ($11.38 diluted EPS) reflect a geopolitical margin spike plus EPA waiver benefits; both could reverse quickly, leaving a higher-cost refiner with much lower normal earnings.
key_risk: Crack spreads normalizing or EPA tightening small-refinery waivers, cutting refining earnings sharply from peak.
catalyst_note: CEO handover to Steve Ledbetter on 1 Jan 2027; Lubricants & Specialties spin-off expected during 2027.

reasons.moat: Cabometyx is a patent-protected blockbuster whose patents were upheld against MSN in Aug 2026, but protection is finite with US generics expected no earlier than January 2030.
reasons.disruption: The patent cliff is roughly four years out and kidney cancer is crowded with checkpoint-inhibitor combinations: a real but not immediate threat.
reasons.industry: Branded specialty oncology has high regulatory and IP barriers and rational pricing; ex-US price controls weigh on partner royalties.
reasons.demand: Cancer drug demand is a secular tailwind; US Cabometyx net revenue reached $603M in Q3 2026, growing on volume and price.
reasons.management: Disciplined, debt-free capital returns ($1.0B of buybacks year to date) with 2026 revenue guidance held at $2.50-2.55B; SG&A growing faster than revenue is a minus.
reasons.tail_risk: About $1.4B of cash and investments and no debt, but roughly 90% of revenue comes from one molecule and the 2030 cliff is approaching.
reasons.catalyst: Zanzalintinib PDUFA date of 3 Mar 2027 in previously treated colorectal cancer and STELLAR-304 kidney cancer topline expected Q1 2027.

bull_case: Cabometyx keeps growing with exclusivity secured to at least 2030 and funds heavy buybacks; approval of zanzalintinib in March 2027 and a kidney-cancer win would make Exelixis a multi-product oncology company before the cliff.
bear_case: Essentially a single-product company facing a 2030 cliff; the FDA already delayed the zanzalintinib decision once, and a rejection or weak STELLAR-304 data would leave no clear replacement.
key_risk: Dependence on cabozantinib ahead of US generic entry around 2030, with the replacement pipeline hinging on zanzalintinib.
catalyst_note: Zanzalintinib PDUFA 3 Mar 2027 (metastatic CRC); STELLAR-304 topline Q1 2027.

reasons.moat: Largest, low-cost independent refiner with complex Gulf Coast plants, but it sells commodity fuels at prices it does not set, so returns track crack spreads.
reasons.disruption: EVs and efficiency erode gasoline demand slowly; renewable diesel (DGD) and ethanol provide a partial hedge.
reasons.industry: US capacity is shrinking (Houston and LA closures in 2025, Benicia in 2026), supporting margins, but refining remains a global price-taking business with new overseas capacity.
reasons.demand: Q3 2026 refining margin of $39.24/bbl was about 3x last year's on geopolitical supply disruption, a likely cyclical peak on top of flat-to-declining long-run fuel demand.
reasons.management: Disciplined: Q3 payouts at 52% of adjusted operating cash flow, St. Charles FCC delivered on time and budget, and the Houston refinery bought far below replacement cost; the March Port Arthur explosion is a blemish.
reasons.tail_risk: Net cash ($9.8B cash vs $8.6B debt), but peak earnings can mean-revert sharply; Port Arthur litigation and California and RFS rules add regulatory risk.
reasons.catalyst: $320.5M Houston refinery purchase expected to close by year-end 2026 with restart by end-2027; modest relative to the margin swing factor.

bull_case: US and West Coast closures plus geopolitical supply shocks keep cracks high for longer, and Valero's low-cost fleet converts that into very large free cash flow and buybacks from a net-cash balance sheet, with a cheap Houston restart adding capacity.
bear_case: Q3 earnings of roughly $24 a share reflect a margin spike that should fade as supply disruptions ease, overstating earnings power at the top of the cycle; demand erosion, outages and regulatory costs remain.
key_risk: Refining margins falling back to normal from a geopolitically driven peak.
catalyst_note: Houston refinery acquisition closes by end-2026, restart targeted by end-2027; Q4 2026 results in early 2027.

reasons.moat: Workflow switching costs, a strong brand, about 18M paying users and roughly 82% gross margins, undercut by Google, Microsoft and Apple bundling comparable storage at little or no cost.
reasons.disruption: AI copilots built into Workspace and Microsoft 365 put the core product at risk; the 10-K itself warns AI could reduce enterprise seats.
reasons.industry: Competes with far larger platform owners that bundle storage for free, leaving standalone vendors little pricing power.
reasons.demand: Q3 revenue grew about 0.5%, ARR fell sequentially to $2.555B, paying-user adds slowed, and the 2027 preview implies flat revenue.
reasons.management: Strong margin discipline (42% non-GAAP operating margin) and guidance raises, offset by founder-CEO and CTO departures, repeated layoffs, a wound-down FormSwift and a new $350M AI-infrastructure bet.
reasons.tail_risk: Debt-funded buybacks left about $2.6B of term loans and a stockholders' deficit on a non-growing revenue base, partly offset by about $1B of free cash flow and diversified customers.
reasons.catalyst: Tigris deal closes in Q4 2026, FY2027 guidance with Q4 results and a CEO transition underway; none clearly decisive.

bull_case: Very high margins and around $1B of free cash flow let buybacks keep growing EPS on flat revenue (diluted shares down from 265M to 225M), with cost cuts and Dash/Tigris offering a possible AI growth leg.
bear_case: Bundled storage and AI assistants are commoditizing the core product while revenue and ARR stall; adding leverage to a no-growth business amid management turnover and an unproven AI bet raises the risk of equity impairment.
key_risk: Paying users and ARR eroding under bundled competitors while leverage stays high.
catalyst_note: Tigris acquisition closes Q4 2026; Q4 results and FY2027 guidance around Feb 2027.

reasons.moat: Largest Williston Basin acreage holder (about 1.3M net acres) with falling costs from 4-mile laterals, but it sells a commodity with no pricing power.
reasons.disruption: Oil faces a slow, real energy-transition threat, which the 10-K flags; nothing replaces the product near term.
reasons.industry: Prices are set globally by OPEC+ and geopolitics, and the 10-K describes intense competition for acreage, services and capital with larger rivals.
reasons.demand: 2026 results ride an oil-price spike (realized $94/bbl in Q2, $86 in Q3 vs a $64 budget deck), a likely cyclical peak, with oil volumes guided lower into Q1 2027.
reasons.management: Strong buybacks ($423M year to date), low debt, about $225M of run-rate savings and a non-core Marcellus sale; offset by an October 2026 CEO change, rising capex and a 2025 goodwill impairment.
reasons.tail_risk: Low net debt (about $1.5B of notes vs $805M cash), but nearly single-basin, reliant on a few pipelines including Dakota Access, and exposed to commodity prices and hedge losses.
reasons.catalyst: $550M Marcellus sale expected to close Q4 2026 and 2027 guidance around February; neither likely to shift the case much.

bull_case: A low-leverage Williston operator that keeps beating volume guidance and cutting well costs, generating about $1.6B of 2026 adjusted free cash flow at elevated prices to fund buybacks and a solid base dividend.
bear_case: Earnings are past the Q2 2026 price peak, volumes are guided lower and capex and operating costs are creeping up; with crude back in the $60s free cash flow falls sharply and no other basin offsets it.
key_risk: Crude prices falling from 2026's elevated levels in a single-basin producer.
catalyst_note: Marcellus divestiture closing expected Q4 2026; 2027 guidance with Q4 results in early 2027.

reasons.moat: Brand, low fixed price points and purchasing scale across about 9,500 stores give a distinct niche, but low-price rivals can contest it and cost pass-through is limited.
reasons.disruption: No meaningful e-commerce while online value sellers and Walmart's omnichannel gain ground; the small-ticket treasure-hunt format slows but does not remove the threat.
reasons.industry: Value retail is highly competitive, with Walmart and Dollar General chasing the same trade-down shopper.
reasons.demand: Higher-income trade-down is a modest tailwind (Q2 comps +3.7%), but traffic grew only 0.4% and mix is shifting to lower-margin consumables: roughly GDP-like.
reasons.management: Sold Family Dollar, beat its own EPS outlook, cut inventory while sales rose, and shrank the share count about 8% in a year through buybacks.
reasons.tail_risk: About 40% of purchases are imported, mostly from China, so tariffs remain live; a September 2026 class action contests its tariff refund; partly offset by about $1.06B of cash.
reasons.catalyst: Q3 FY26 results on 24 Nov 2026 will show whether comps hold at 3-4% and margins survive once tariff-refund effects are stripped out.

bull_case: Standalone after the Family Dollar sale, Dollar Tree is beating guidance, multi-price items have grown to 17% of sales, traffic is positive and strong free cash flow funds buybacks; FY26 EPS guidance of $7.70-8.05 may have room to rise.
bear_case: Part of the 2026 earnings jump rests on a one-time tariff refund now contested in court, management expects Q4 gross margin pressure, and Walmart and Dollar General fight hard for the same shopper.
key_risk: China tariff and sourcing exposure with limited pricing room squeezing margins once the refund benefit fades.
catalyst_note: Q3 FY2026 earnings and outlook update on 24 Nov 2026.

reasons.moat: Scale in licensed healthcare education (Chamberlain nursing, Walden, Ross/AUC medical and veterinary) plus accreditation and hospital clinical partnerships give real but contestable barriers.
reasons.disruption: Pre-licensure nursing and medical training require clinical placements and licensure, which are hard to substitute.
reasons.industry: Competes with nonprofit, public and large online universities; regulation limits entry, but federal aid caps constrain pricing.
reasons.demand: Nurse and physician shortages support multi-year demand; Walden enrollment up 12.8% while Chamberlain (+1.3%) and Med/Vet (+3.5%) are slowing.
reasons.management: Has beaten and raised guidance and cut diluted shares from 37.1M to 34.6M at about 0.5x net leverage; minus points for excluding recurring advisory costs from adjusted results and a CFO retirement.
reasons.tail_risk: Low leverage (net debt about $288M) but heavy reliance on federal student aid; loan caps effective July 2026 already weigh on Med/Vet, plus legacy litigation and for-profit regulatory history.
reasons.catalyst: Fiscal Q2 2027 results around early February (guided softer on a Walden calendar shift), a new CFO appointment and a Nashville campus opening in January: near-term but modest.

bull_case: Healthcare workforce shortages and hospital partnerships support steady enrollment and margin growth; the FY27-29 plan targets 6-11% revenue and 9-16% adjusted EPS growth with buybacks shrinking the share count.
bear_case: New federal loan caps could keep slowing Chamberlain and Med/Vet enrollment, leaving growth reliant on Walden online; rising credit-loss provisions, the CFO change and reliance on adjusted earnings could compress the valuation.
key_risk: Federal aid changes (Grad PLUS removed, professional loans capped) cutting medical-school enrollment and pricing.
catalyst_note: Fiscal Q2 2027 results around early February 2027 and the new CFO appointment.

reasons.moat: Well-known names (Macy's, Bloomingdale's, the parade) and prime real estate, but a multibrand apparel retailer has little pricing power or switching cost.
reasons.disruption: E-commerce, off-price chains and direct-to-consumer brands keep taking share from mid-tier mall department stores.
reasons.industry: Fragmented and promotional apparel and beauty market; distressed rivals such as Saks Global (Chapter 11 since January 2026) free up share but do not bring rational pricing.
reasons.demand: Mid-tier department stores are in structural decline; FY26 guides comps of only +1.0-1.5%, with growth concentrated at Bloomingdale's and Bluemercury.
reasons.management: The 'Bold New Chapter' plan is closing about 150 stores, reinvesting in core stores and raising guidance with buybacks, offset by the 2024 hidden-expense restatement and activist pressure.
reasons.tail_risk: $1.3B cash and $2.4B debt with no material maturities until 2030, but exposed to consumer cyclicality and tariffs; Q2 margins were helped by one-time tariff refunds.
reasons.catalyst: Q3 results in early December and holiday results around March are routine; real-estate monetization or a Bloomingdale's/Bluemercury separation has no set timing.

bull_case: The turnaround is working: comps turned positive, Bloomingdale's is gaining share as Saks retreats, the balance sheet has no material maturities until 2030, and FY26 adjusted EPS guidance of $2.15-2.35 plus buybacks looks cheap.
bear_case: The core Macy's nameplate grows about 1% in a channel in long-term decline; Q2 was flattered by one-time tariff refunds, and a weaker value-conscious consumer or renewed tariffs could undo margin gains.
key_risk: Structural share loss at the core Macy's nameplate amid consumer and tariff swings.
catalyst_note: Q3 FY2026 results in early December 2026 and holiday/FY2027 guidance around March 2027.
